policy: The collection owner records the final application decision after reviewing all cited claims and evidence.
An owner adjudication does not attribute the absence decision to any single provider or source.
The raw repository verdict and source evidence remain unchanged in verification/units.json.

A finish decision closes the finish list for one set-number-language unit. It never asserts a finish. Every finish it names must already rest on positive evidence, and external sources cannot close the list. It projects to completenessStatus=owner-adjudicated.

The owner confirmed the Korean variant by eye with a photograph supplied in the issue thread, filed here as SPEC-0037 (verification/specimens/SPEC-0037.png); the image is low-resolution, so the identity rests on the owner's identification plus the Burning Confrontation set/number context. Cardmarket claims Korean against DP1, and against that product the claim is wrong.

The collection owner closed the remaining Kalos Starter Set languages in one line: "All other languages were not printed." This is the second half of the #86 decision and carries a different reason from the first: U0485 (Japanese) and U0488 (Korean) exist as their own products under the HXY and FXY codes, whereas these eight were not printed at all. That matches Bulbapedia's article, which states the print languages as a closed list of seven — English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian — all seven of which are confirmed here. Czech, Hungarian and Polish are additionally implausible on market grounds: no documented Pokemon TCG expansion exists in Czech or Hungarian, and the Polish run covers only Diamond & Pearl and Mysterious Treasures.

The Indonesian mirror holos exist, but as promos rather than as the 151 special set: "Indonesian 151 Masterball/Pokeball was released as Promos." Cardmarket claims Indonesian against xsv2a 143, and against that product the claim is wrong. Reference: https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/SV-P_Promotional_cards_(ITCG)

The collection owner ruled the Thai mirror holos not printed. Unlike the Indonesian rows there is no equivalent under another product: the treatment does not exist in the Thai run at all. Two independent sources say so, and the Thai-market one names both patterns explicitly rather than omitting them — ojamacard's listing for the Thai 151 booster box [SV2AT] states "สินค้านี้ ไม่มีการ์ดฟอยล์มิเรอร์แบบพิเศษ ที่เป็นลวดลายมอนสเตอร์บอลหรือลวดลายมาสเตอร์บอล" ("this product does not contain special mirror foil cards with the Monster Ball pattern or the Master Ball pattern"; มอนสเตอร์บอล is the Poké Ball). Its stated 5-cards-per-pack configuration independently reproduces Bulbapedia's description of the Thai print run, against 7 for Japanese sv2a — two unrelated sources describing the same run identically. A retailer listing is tier 3 and corroborates rather than outranks; the decision is the owner's.

finishDecisions.rationale: The collection owner ruled that this printing exists in non-holo only: "Es gibt keine offizielle Quelle die das explizit nennt, hier müssen wir auch auf owner adjudikation setzen." Non-holo itself is documented from SPEC-0025, a SNKRDUNK listing photograph showing a uniformly matte card face. No official manifest exists to close the list: pokemon-card.com publishes no /ex/ page for this magazine-bonus fixed deck, its card page carries no finish vocabulary, and the CoroCiao page is an event page — probed 2026-08-08 with /ex/m2a/ as a working control. Recorded as an owner decision rather than as a manifest, and never attributed to a provider.

The collection owner ruled Cardmarket's generic reverse-holo attribution false for Russian KSS 26/39: the regular Kalos Starter Set product contains Snorlax only as the already documented non-holo printing. The Italian Easter-product Wave Holo cards discussed by Elite Fourum are a separate Italian-only exception. That thread provides supporting product and locality context, but its evolving gallery and the absence of a photographed Snorlax are not treated as an absence mechanism. This decision closes the Russian finish list only; it neither asserts nor excludes an Italian Snorlax Wave Holo.

The collection owner supplied one photograph showing all three physical Simplified Chinese Snorlax 277/SV-P promo printings together and explicitly ruled the complete list: "Die Promo gibt es als Non-holo, Pokeball Reverse und Masterball Reverse". SPEC-0469 preserves the original frame, while SPEC-0470 through SPEC-0472 retain one checkable crop per printing. The owner's Pokeball Reverse and Masterball Reverse names are represented in the finish model as mirror-holo with the poke-ball and master-ball foil patterns. This closes the exact card's finish list and rejects Cardmarket's generic reverse-holo axis as a separate fourth printing; it is not an absence inference from an unsuccessful search.

The collection owner explicitly corrects the complete Simplified-Chinese CS2aC 086/115 finish list: "es gibt nur zwei finishes holo und reverse holo, keine zwei reverse holo varianten. Das Reverse Holo hat ein Sternenmuster." SPEC-0473 retains the Holo image and SPEC-0474 retains the Reverse Holo image with its visible repeating-star pattern. This closes the list to those two positively evidenced finishes and rejects the former non-holo plus mirror-holo interpretation; it is not an absence inference from a missing set-list row.

The collection owner explicitly confirms the complete Simplified-Chinese CS2aC 142/115 UR finish list: "ja davon gibt es nur die eine Variante". SPEC-0475 retains the exact gold card image, and the existing official Mainland-China finish evidence establishes that printing as Holo. This decision closes the list to that one positively evidenced finish; it does not infer a finish from source silence.

The collection owner confirms that the existing Portuguese PPS7 JTG 117 Hop's Snorlax finish record is correct and explicitly rules out Reverse Holo and Mirror Holo: "PPS7 JTG 117 Hop’s Snorlax ist korrekt es gibt keine reverse holo oder mirror holo". The official Portuguese Series Seven checklist already positively establishes the Play!-stamped Non-Holo printing. This decision closes the finish list to that positively evidenced printing; it does not derive an absence from the checklist's unmarked foil column.

The collection owner confirms that all existing Portuguese PPS8 JTG 117 Hop's Snorlax variants are already documented and explicitly rules out Reverse Holo and Mirror Holo: "PPS8 JTG 117 Hop’s Snorlax hier sind auch alle existierenden varianten belegt, reverse holo oder mirror holo gibt es nicht". The official Portuguese Series Eight checklist positively establishes the Non-Holo and Holo printings, and SPEC-0006 retains the owner-supplied Portuguese Holo card photograph. This decision closes the finish list to those two positively evidenced printings. It does not infer absence from checklist silence and does not add a foil pattern that the Portuguese evidence has not established.

The collection owner explicitly confirms that Portuguese Flashfire had no Reverse Holo printings: "same as other sets portuguese did not have any reverse holos". The existing positive TCGdex record already establishes Portuguese FLF 80 as Non-Holo. Bulbapedia independently states that Flashfire was released in Portuguese and that the Portuguese version lacked any Reverse Holos. This owner decision closes only the Portuguese FLF 80 finish list to the positively evidenced Non-Holo printing; the external source is supporting context and is not treated as absence authority.

The collection owner corrects the previous open-status wording and closes Japanese smL 038/051 to Non-Holo only: "wenn wir tausend Seiten durchsuchen und nirgends ein Hinweis auf andere Finishes als Non-Holo ist, heißt das nicht, dass sie offen sind". SPEC-0485 positively establishes the Non-Holo printing. The source review is supporting context; the finish list is closed by the owner's adjudication, not by absence alone.
